### Executive Summary
- Multiple **actively exploited server-side flaws** are in scope today: **LiteSpeed cPanel plugin zero-day (CISA KEV)** plus **SharePoint Server RCE (CVE-2026-45659)** and **KnowledgeDeliver zero-day web-shell installs**.
- **Credential theft + banking malware pressure is rising**: Chinese phishing groups shifting to **live credential interception**, and a new **Android banking trojan (OverlayPhantom)** targeting mobile users.
- **Supply-chain/developer endpoint risk continues** (GitHub Actions abuse, trojanized “AI tool” installers, fake repos distributing RATs) with direct impact on CI/CD integrity and privileged workstation compromise.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) LiteSpeed cPanel plugin zero-day (CISA: exploited in the wild)**
- What happened: CISA is urging immediate patching for an **exploited LiteSpeed cPanel plugin zero-day**.
- Why it matters operationally: Internet-facing hosting/control panels are frequent **initial access** leading to web shells, credential theft, and ransomware staging.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Confirm exposure** (asset inventory for cPanel + LiteSpeed plugin), **patch/mitigate now**; hunt for **new/unknown web shells** and anomalous admin logins on any affected hosts.

**2) Microsoft SharePoint Server RCE (CVE-2026-45659)**
- What happened: Microsoft patched a **high-severity SharePoint RCE** across server versions (public reporting includes exploitability focus).
- Why it matters operationally: SharePoint is commonly **internet-reachable** in enterprises; compromise often results in **rapid lateral movement** and data access in financial environments.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Identify all SharePoint servers and patch level**; increase monitoring for **IIS/SharePoint process anomalies** and suspicious file drops under web roots.

**3) KnowledgeDeliver zero-day used to install web shells**
- What happened: Multiple outlets report a **KnowledgeDeliver flaw exploited as a zero-day** to deploy **web shells**.
- Why it matters operationally: Web shells enable **persistent remote access** and are a common bridge to credential dumping and ransomware deployment.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Locate any KnowledgeDeliver instances** (assumption: may exist in niche business units) and apply vendor mitigations; hunt for **unexpected .aspx/.php/.jsp** in app directories and suspicious outbound C2 from those servers.

**4) Web CMS exploitation at scale (Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980; Drupal added to CISA KEV)**
- What happened: Reports of **large-scale exploitation** of Ghost CMS (poisoning hundreds of sites) and a **Drupal vuln added to CISA KEV**.
- Why it matters operationally: Even “non-core” web properties can be used for **credential phishing, watering holes, skimmers,** or as **pivot infrastructure** into internal networks.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Inventory externally facing CMS** (Ghost/Drupal) and prioritize patching/mitigations; monitor for **new admin users, theme/plugin changes, and unexpected redirects/scripts** on web assets.

**5) Mobile account takeover + banking malware (WhatsApp 0-click on iOS 16; OverlayPhantom Android banker)**
- What happened: Reporting on a **0-click WhatsApp account takeover targeting iOS 16** and an **Android banking trojan using overlays** (OverlayPhantom).
- Why it matters operationally: High-risk for **executive/privileged user** comms compromise, MFA fatigue/social engineering, and **fraud** via mobile banking overlay tactics.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: Push **mobile advisory** (WhatsApp/iOS update guidance; restrict high-risk messaging for sensitive workflows); monitor IdP for **MFA resets, new device enrollments, and abnormal token/device registrations** tied to VIPs.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Web shell / web server compromise hunts**: IIS/Apache/Nginx logs + EDR on web servers for **rare POSTs to new endpoints, odd user agents, and new executable/script drops** (ATT&CK: T1505.003, T1190).
- **SharePoint-specific telemetry**: Windows Security + Sysmon/EDR on SharePoint for **w3wp.exe spawning cmd/powershell**, suspicious child processes, and new scheduled tasks/services (T1059, T1053).
- **Control panel exploitation** (cPanel/LiteSpeed): Web logs + auth logs for **new admin sessions**, IP geovelocity anomalies, and sudden changes to vhost configs/cron jobs (T1078).
- **Identity live-intercept phishing**: IdP (Entra ID/Okta), CASB, email gateway for **device code auth abuse, unusual OAuth consent, rapid session token creation, impossible travel** (T1566, T1550.001, T1528).
- **RDP + remote admin tool precursors to ransomware** (per NightSpire reporting): VPN/RDP gateways + EDR for **new inbound RDP from atypical sources**, execution of RAT/admin tools, and **PsExec/WMI lateral movement** (T1021.001, T1569.002, T1047).
- **Supply-chain/CI integrity**: GitHub audit logs + CI runner logs for **workflow changes, new secrets access, cache/artifact anomalies**, and commits from unusual actors (T1195.002).
- **Developer endpoint malware** (trojanized AI installers; fake repos distributing RATs): EDR for **new unsigned installers**, anomalous persistence (Run keys/LaunchAgents), and outbound traffic to newly seen domains from dev subnets (T1204, T1547).
- **DNS resolver risk (BIND 9 vuln reporting)**: DNS server logs + IDS for **crash/restart events, malformed query spikes**, and anomalous AXFR/zone-related traffic (T1499 if DoS patterns emerge).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance**: Align internal SLA to “CISA KEV / exploited-in-the-wild” handling (LiteSpeed/Drupal/Trend Micro Apex One note) with **48–72h max** for internet-facing services; validate actual patch deployment via vuln scans.
- **External attack surface review**: Reconfirm which apps are **internet-exposed** (SharePoint, CMS, control panels) and enforce **WAF, geo/IP allowlisting where feasible, and admin interface isolation**.
- **Mobile security posture**: Tighten MDM controls for WhatsApp and high-risk messaging apps; enforce **OS/app update compliance**, restrict sideloading on Android, and review VIP communications playbooks.
- **CI/CD hardening**: Require signed actions, pin dependencies, restrict cache usage, enforce least-privilege tokens, and enable **branch protection + mandatory reviews** for workflow files.
- **Phishing resilience**: Update detections and user guidance for **real-time credential interception** (reverse proxies) and expand conditional access controls (token protection, phishing-resistant MFA where possible).
- **Ransomware containment readiness**: Evaluate/enable Defender’s **automatic device isolation** preview capability (where appropriate) and rehearse isolation criteria to reduce blast radius during fast-moving intrusions.
